ideas.title: Why the Octopus Changes Color in a Split Second #Shorts
ideas.concept: Explain how octopus skin cells (chromatophores) let it instantly camouflage for hunting and hiding.
ideas.hook: Watch this octopus vanish… it’s not magic—it’s living pixels.
ideas.keyVisual: Close-up stock footage of an octopus on reef rock rapidly shifting from mottled brown to bright/striped patterns while moving.

ideas.title: Why the Hummingbird Can Hover Like a Helicopter #Shorts
ideas.concept: Break down the unique wingbeat motion that allows hovering and flying backward.
ideas.hook: This bird can stop midair and even fly backwards—here’s the trick.
ideas.keyVisual: High-speed style clip of a hummingbird hovering at a flower, then reversing slightly and repositioning.

ideas.title: Why the Crocodile Can Hold Its Breath for Over an Hour #Shorts
ideas.concept: Teach the simple physiology (slow metabolism + efficient oxygen use) behind long underwater ambushes.
ideas.hook: A crocodile can wait underwater longer than you can watch this video.
ideas.keyVisual: Crocodile barely submerged at water surface with only eyes/nose visible, then slow underwater glide toward prey area.

ideas.title: 5 Animal Superpowers That Sound Made Up
ideas.concept: Pilot long-form episode. Not a raw compilation — new narration, cold open, bridges, and pacing built from the week's best Shorts footage. Features dolphin (half-brain sleep), turtle (butt breathing), bear (20-mile smell), lion (5-mile roar), and tiger (6x night vision). All are survival superpowers, not just senses.
ideas.hook: These animals have abilities that sound completely fake — but every single one is real.
ideas.keyVisual: Split-screen composite of 5 animal faces (dolphin, turtle, bear, lion, tiger) with bold 'SUPERPOWERS' text overlay

episodeStructure.title: Tiger — Sees 6x Better in the Dark

episodeStructure.narration: Recap + subscribe CTA — '5 real superpowers. Which one amazed you most? Subscribe for weekly wildlife episodes.'

longFormPlan.concept: Weekly long-form episode built FROM Shorts assets — not a raw compilation. Each episode features 5-7 animal segments from the week's best Shorts, but with entirely new narration, cold open, transitions, pacing, and chapter structure. Feels like an original mini-doc, not stitched-together Shorts.
longFormPlan.rationale: Long-form videos earn watch hours toward YPP (currently 127.8/4000 = 3.2%), reach broader audiences beyond Shorts feed, and rank in YouTube search. Reusing footage from Shorts keeps production cost low while new narration and structure make it original content.
longFormPlan.cadence: Weekly — Sunday production, published Sunday evening
longFormPlan.validationStrategy: Pilot first, automate later. Build one semi-manual episode, track CTR, average view duration, total watch hours, subscribers gained, and whether Shorts viewers cross over to long-form. If retention holds, automate the weekly flow. If weak, pivot to original mini-docs.

format.structure: Cold open hook (15s) → 5-7 segments with 5-10s bridging narration between each → recap + subscribe CTA (20s)
transformations: New cold open narration (not reused from any Short)
Remove repeated intros/outros from Short segments
New bridging narration between segments (thematic connective tissue)
Tighter pacing — trim weak moments from original Shorts
Chapter timestamps in description for each animal
format.thumbnail: Composite of top 3 animal faces with bold text overlay

productionFlow: 1. Read pulse-snapshot.json + producer-analytics.json to select top 5-7 Shorts from past 7 days (prioritize WINNER labels)
2. Source each Short's footage clips from workspace cache (prerequisite: durable storage)
3. Write new episode script: cold open + bridges + outro (150-250 words of NEW narration)
4. Generate TTS for new narration segments only
5. Assemble with ffmpeg: cold open → segment 1 → bridge → segment 2 → bridge → ... → outro
6. Add chapter markers and upload as standard video (not Shorts)
prerequisites: Cache Short footage clips to workspace (currently in /tmp which clears between runs)
New assembly script supporting episode mode (cold open + segments + bridges + outro)
New TTS script generation for episode narration

yppImpact.watchHoursPerWeek: ~1.5-2 hours per episode (6-8 min × 15-25 views in first week)
yppImpact.note: Long-form watch hours compound — videos keep getting views over months. Real impact likely 2-3x first-week numbers.

risks: YouTube may flag reused Shorts footage as repurposed content — mitigated by new narration, pacing, and chapter structure
Retention may be lower than Shorts (viewers accustomed to 60s content) — mitigated by strong cold open and tight pacing
Production complexity higher than Shorts — mitigated by starting with semi-manual pilot before automating
